items.passage:
Dear Ms. Whitfield,

I am writing on behalf of the Elmwood Community Choir, a group of thirty amateur singers who have rehearsed in the basement of St. Lorne Hall for the past six years. As you may know, the hall is scheduled to close for structural repairs from early March until the end of August, and we have been searching, so far without success, for a space large enough to accommodate us. Several of our members have pointed out that the multipurpose room at Brookside Library, which I understand stands empty on Thursday evenings, might suit our needs perfectly. We would be grateful if you would consider allowing us to use the room from 7 to 9 p.m. each Thursday during those six months. We are, of course, prepared to pay the standard rental fee, to set up and restore the furniture ourselves, and to keep our volume at a level that will not disturb library patrons. In return, we would be delighted to offer a free concert for the library's summer reading celebration. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Daniel Okafor
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 공사 기간 동안 도서관 다목적실 대여를 요청하려고
연습 장소의 보수 공사 일정 연기를 요청하려고
도서관 여름 독서 행사의 자원봉사를 신청하려고
다목적실 대여료를 낮춰 줄 것을 요청하려고
items.exp: 연습하던 홀이 3월부터 8월까지 보수 공사로 문을 닫으니 그동안 목요일 저녁에 도서관 다목적실을 쓰게 해 달라고 부탁하는 편지예요. 무료 공연은 대여를 허락해 주면 보답으로 하겠다는 제안일 뿐이고, 대여료는 정상 요금을 내겠다고 했어요.

items.passage: The email from my editor arrived at 11:52 p.m., its subject line a single phrase: 'Chapter One.' I stared at it without opening it. For three months I had wrestled with the novel's first chapter, an elderly fisherman's monologue full of a dialect I had never heard spoken aloud. Every sentence I had rendered into English felt like a guess dressed up as a decision. I imagined the message beginning with a polite paragraph of praise before the inevitable 'however.' My fingers hovered over the trackpad, and my heart was thudding so loudly that I could hear it over the hum of the refrigerator. Finally I clicked. 'I read it twice,' she had written, 'and the second time I forgot it was a translation. The old man's voice is exactly right—gruff, funny, heartbreaking. Don't change a thing. Send me chapter two whenever you're ready.' I read the lines again, then a third time, and laughed out loud in my empty kitchen. The knot that had sat in my stomach since spring slowly loosened.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 I의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 처음에는 메일을 열지 못하고 '하지만'으로 이어질 비판을 상상하며 심장이 쿵쾅거릴 만큼 불안해했어요. 편집자의 칭찬을 읽은 뒤에는 웃음이 터지고 뱃속의 매듭이 풀렸으니 안도한 거예요.

items.passage: When we disagree with someone in a public discussion, our instinct is to identify the weakest point in their position and attack it. This produces a satisfying sense of victory, but it rarely changes anyone's mind, least of all the mind of the person we are arguing with. People who feel that their views have been caricatured tend to dig in, interpreting our rebuttal as proof that we have not understood them. A more productive habit is to begin any response by restating the opposing view in its strongest form—so accurately and generously that its holder might say, 'Yes, that is exactly what I mean, and you put it better than I did.' Only then should we explain where we think it goes wrong. This practice is demanding; it forces us to engage with reasons we would rather dismiss, and it occasionally reveals that our own position is less secure than we had assumed. Yet that discomfort is precisely the point. Debates conducted this way may produce fewer dramatic wins, but they leave participants better informed and far more willing to keep talking.
items.q: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 반박하기 전에 상대의 견해를 가장 강한 형태로 먼저 정리해야 한다.
공개 토론에서는 상대 주장의 약점을 빠르게 찾아내야 한다.
토론에서는 감정보다 논리적 근거를 앞세워야 한다.
자신의 견해가 틀렸다면 즉시 인정해야 한다.
토론의 목적은 승패가 아니라 합의 도출이어야 한다.
items.exp: 상대의 약점을 공격하기보다, 상대가 '바로 그 뜻'이라고 할 만큼 그 견해를 가장 강한 형태로 다시 말한 뒤에 반박하라는 것이 필자의 주장이에요. ②는 필자가 비판하는 본능이고, ⑤의 합의 도출은 글에서 말하지 않았어요.

items.passage: Organizations love numbers because numbers can be tracked, compared, and rewarded. A hospital that wants shorter waiting times measures the minutes between a patient's arrival and the first contact with staff. A school that wants better learning counts the proportion of students who pass a standardized test. The trouble begins when the number stops being a window onto the condition it was meant to reveal and becomes the target itself. Staff quickly discover that a nurse can greet patients within minutes without beginning treatment any sooner, and that teachers can rehearse the test format rather than deepen understanding. The figures improve; the realities they were supposed to reflect do not. In such cases the institution is, in effect, [polishing the thermometer] while the fever continues untouched. The remedy is not to abandon measurement, which remains indispensable, but to rotate indicators, combine them with direct observation, and remember that any figure is a symptom to be interpreted rather than a goal to be maximized.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [polishing the thermometer]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: replacing outdated tools with more precise instruments
hiding unfavorable results from public inspection
improving the indicator without improving the underlying condition
relying on intuition instead of objective data
treating short-term problems while ignoring long-term causes
items.exp: 체온계(지표)만 닦고 열(실제 상태)은 그대로 둔다는 뜻으로, 수치는 좋아지지만 그 수치가 반영해야 할 현실은 나아지지 않는 상황을 가리켜요. 결과를 숨기는 것(②)이 아니라 수치 자체가 실제로 좋아지는 점이 핵심이에요.

items.passage: Look at the Moon through a modest telescope and you will see a face pitted with thousands of craters, some of them billions of years old. Earth, which orbits in the same neighborhood and has been struck by at least as many objects, displays only around two hundred confirmed impact structures. The difference has little to do with luck. Our planet is geologically restless: wind, rain, and flowing water wear down crater rims within a few million years, while sediment gradually fills the remaining basins. More fundamentally, the slow movement of tectonic plates drags old ocean floor back into the mantle, erasing whatever scars it carried. Even the atmosphere plays a part, causing many smaller bodies to burn up or break apart before they reach the ground. The Moon, lacking air, water, and active plates, simply keeps every wound it has ever received. In this sense, Earth's apparently unblemished surface is less a sign of safety than a record of constant renewal—a history continuously rewritten rather than preserved.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: methods scientists use to date craters on the Moon
the threat that asteroid impacts pose to life on Earth
the role of the atmosphere in protecting orbiting satellites
differences in the number of objects striking Earth and the Moon
reasons why Earth's surface keeps so few traces of impacts
items.exp: 지구도 달만큼 충돌을 겪었지만 풍화·퇴적, 판의 움직임, 대기 때문에 충돌 흔적이 지워지거나 생기지 않는다는 내용이에요. ④는 지구도 적어도 그만큼 충돌을 겪었다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: Before the late nineteenth century, time was a local affair. Each town set its clocks by the position of the sun, so that noon in one city might arrive several minutes before noon in another only a short distance to the west. For most people this hardly mattered; few traveled far enough or fast enough to notice. The railways changed that. A train crossing a region could pass through dozens of local times in a single journey, and timetables became bewildering lists of conversions. Worse, confusion about when a train was due could place two trains on the same track at the same moment. Railway companies therefore began to adopt shared standard times along their lines, and in 1883 the major North American railroads coordinated a system of time zones that most cities soon followed. What had begun as a technical convenience for engineers gradually became the common rhythm of everyday life, and today the idea that the hour on our watch should match the hour hundreds of kilometers away seems so natural that we forget it was ever invented.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: When the Sun Ruled the Clock: Life Before Railways
How Trains Put a Whole Region on One Clock
Faster Trains, Safer Tracks: An Engineering Revolution
Why Local Time Was More Accurate Than Standard Time
The Hidden Costs of Global Time Zones
items.exp: 마을마다 해를 기준으로 시각을 정하던 시대에 철도가 혼란과 사고 위험을 낳자 철도 회사들이 표준시와 시간대를 도입했고, 이것이 일상의 시간이 되었다는 내용이에요. ①은 철도 이전 시기만 다루어 글의 중심인 표준시의 탄생을 담지 못해요.

items.passage: Ilse Marbach (1891–1967) was a ceramic artist whose work helped bring folk pottery techniques into modern design. Born in a small village in northern Bavaria, she spent her childhood in her uncle's workshop, where she learned to throw pots before she could read fluently. At nineteen she moved to Vienna to study sculpture, but she soon grew dissatisfied with what she called 'clay that is only looked at' and returned to functional ware. In 1924 she opened a studio that trained young women, many of whom later ran workshops of their own. Marbach became known for her ash glazes, which she produced by burning local plants and testing hundreds of combinations, recording each result in notebooks that survive today. Although her tableware won a gold medal at an international exhibition in 1937, she refused most commissions from wealthy collectors, insisting that her bowls belonged on ordinary kitchen tables. She continued working until a hand injury forced her to stop at the age of seventy-two.
items.q: 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: 어린 시절 삼촌의 작업장에서 도자기 빚는 법을 배웠다.
열아홉 살에 빈으로 가서 조각을 공부했다.
재를 이용한 유약 실험 결과를 기록한 노트가 남아 있다.
items.exp: 그녀는 자신의 그릇이 평범한 부엌 식탁에 있어야 한다며 부유한 수집가들의 주문을 대부분 거절했어요. 나머지는 삼촌의 작업장, 열아홉 살의 빈 유학, 1924년 작업실, 남아 있는 노트 내용과 일치해요.

items.passage: Young children learning English often produce words they have never heard, such as 'goed' or 'mouses.' At first glance these errors seem to be signs of backward progress, especially since the same children may have correctly said 'went' a few months earlier. Linguists, however, view them as evidence of a remarkable achievement. A child who says 'goed' ①[have extracted] a general rule—add '-ed' to show the past—from thousands of examples, ②[none of which] was ever explained to her. Having discovered the rule, she applies it everywhere, including to the irregular verbs she had previously memorized as isolated items. The temporary errors, in other words, reveal a shift from imitation to construction. Eventually, through repeated exposure to adult speech, the child learns which words ③[resist] the pattern, and the correct irregular forms return, this time ④[stored] as exceptions to a rule rather than as random facts. Parents ⑤[worrying] about such mistakes can be reassured: the mistakes themselves are a sign that grammar is being built, not lost.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: 주어가 단수인 A child(who says 'goed')이므로 동사는 have extracted가 아니라 has extracted가 되어야 해요. ②는 thousands of examples를 받는 관계대명사, ③은 복수 주어 which words에 맞는 동사, ④는 형태가 '저장된' 의미의 분사, ⑤는 Parents를 꾸미는 현재분사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside. Dark asphalt and roofing materials absorb sunlight and ①[release] the stored heat slowly into the evening air, while the scarcity of trees ②[removes] the cooling effect of shade and evaporation. One proposed remedy is surprisingly simple: paint roofs white or cover them with reflective coatings. A light surface returns much of the incoming sunlight to the sky, keeping both the building and the air above it ③[cooler]. Studies have found that such roofs can noticeably ④[raise] the energy needed for air conditioning in the buildings beneath them. The approach is not without limitations. In cities with cold winters, a reflective roof may slightly increase heating costs, and its benefits ⑤[fade] as dirt accumulates on the surface unless it is cleaned regularly. Planners therefore treat cool roofs as one tool among several, to be combined with street trees, green spaces, and building materials suited to the local climate.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 밝은 지붕은 햇빛을 반사해 건물을 시원하게 하므로 냉방에 필요한 에너지를 줄여야 해요. 그래서 raise를 reduce로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 열을 천천히 방출함, 나무 부족이 그늘 효과를 없앰, 더 시원함, 먼지로 효과가 줄어듦으로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: A professional tennis serve can travel at more than 200 kilometers per hour, reaching the receiver in roughly half a second. Given the time required to perceive the ball, decide on a response, and move the body, a player who waited to see where the ball was going would simply be too late. Elite returners succeed not because their reactions are dramatically faster than everyone else's—laboratory tests show surprisingly modest differences—but because they begin to act before the ball is even struck. Eye-tracking studies reveal that experts look at different places than novices do: rather than following the ball, they focus on the server's hips, shoulders, and racket angle, extracting cues that signal the likely direction of the shot. In other words, their advantage lies largely in ___. This also explains why skilled players are vulnerable to opponents who disguise their movements; a server who can produce identical body positions for different serves takes away the very information on which the returner's early response depends.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 뛰어난 리시버는 반응 속도가 빨라서가 아니라 공이 맞기도 전에 상대의 몸 단서를 읽고 미리 움직이므로, 강점은 '예측'에 있어요. 반응 속도 차이는 크지 않다고 했으니 reflexes는 답이 될 수 없어요.

items.passage: Imagine two paintings that no expert, using any available technique, can tell apart: one was painted by a celebrated seventeenth-century master, the other by a skilled forger last year. If aesthetic value lay entirely in what we see, the two works should be equally valuable, and the outrage that follows the discovery of a forgery would be a kind of snobbery. Yet most of us feel that something real is lost when a beloved picture is unmasked as a fake, even though not a single brushstroke has changed. The reason, many philosophers argue, is that we never respond to an artwork as a mere arrangement of colors. We respond to it as an achievement—as the solution to problems that a particular person faced at a particular moment, with the materials and conventions then available. A daring use of light that was revolutionary in 1650 is merely skillful imitation today. What we admire, then, is inseparable from ___, and that is exactly what the forgery cannot share with the original, however perfect its surface.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the visual qualities that experts can detect on the surface
the price the work commands in the art market
the emotional response it produces in each viewer
the history of how the work came to be made
the technical skill required to reproduce its appearance
items.exp: 우리는 작품을 특정 인물이 특정 시기에 문제를 해결한 성취로 감상하므로, 감탄의 대상은 작품이 만들어진 내력과 떼어 놓을 수 없어요. 위작도 높은 기술(⑤)과 똑같은 표면(①)은 가질 수 있으니 원작과 다른 점이 될 수 없어요.

items.passage: Peer tutoring is usually justified by what it does for the student who receives help, but research suggests that the tutor often gains just as much. ① Preparing to explain a topic forces tutors to organize their knowledge, filling gaps they had not noticed while studying alone. ② When a younger learner asks an unexpected question, the tutor must reconstruct the reasoning behind a procedure rather than simply repeating it. ③ This process deepens understanding in ways that rereading a textbook or reviewing notes seldom does, because it turns passive recognition into active explanation. ④ Schools that adopt tutoring programs, however, often struggle to find enough trained adult tutors, especially in rural areas where qualified teachers are already scarce. ⑤ Tutors also report greater confidence and a stronger sense of responsibility for their own learning, since they now feel accountable to someone who depends on them, and many continue to study the subject more diligently long after the program has ended.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 글은 또래 가르치기가 가르치는 학생에게 주는 이익(지식 정리, 추론 재구성, 이해 심화, 자신감과 책임감)을 다루어요. ④는 성인 튜터를 구하기 어렵다는 학교의 운영 문제로 흐름에서 벗어나요.

items.passage:
Whenever data travels from one computer to another, some bits inevitably get flipped along the way by electrical noise or interference, so that a 0 arrives as a 1 or vice versa. A system that cannot notice such changes will simply pass corrupted information along as if nothing had happened.

(A) The receiver performs the same count on what it gets. If the total is no longer even, it knows that something went wrong and can ask for the data to be sent again. This trick, however, has an obvious limit: if two bits flip at once, the count comes out even again, and the error slips through unnoticed.

(B) One of the simplest defenses is called a parity bit. Before sending a group of bits, the sender counts how many 1s it contains and attaches one extra bit, chosen so that the total number of 1s is always even.

(C) For this reason, modern systems rely on more elaborate codes that add several extra bits in carefully designed positions. These codes can not only detect multiple errors but often locate and repair them without any retransmission at all.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 먼저 방어책인 패리티 비트를 소개하는 (B)가 오고, 송신자와 '같은 계산'을 수신자가 한다는 (A)가 이어져요. (A) 끝의 '두 비트가 동시에 바뀌면 못 잡는다'는 한계를 For this reason으로 받아 더 정교한 코드를 소개하는 (C)가 마지막이에요.

items.passage: Across cultures, gifts rarely come free. Receiving one creates a sense of obligation, and much of social life is woven from the timing and manner in which that obligation is repaid. ( ① ) In some communities, people are expected to reciprocate quickly and precisely, so that a dinner invitation is answered with a dinner of similar cost within a few weeks. ( ② ) Elsewhere, however, the point of a gift is to keep a relationship open rather than to settle it. ( ③ ) And closing the account is precisely what nobody wants, since it signals that one wishes to be free of the giver, ending the very bond the gift was meant to sustain. ( ④ ) Anthropologists have observed that in many such societies, a slightly unequal exchange, with one side always a little in debt, keeps people visiting, helping, and remembering one another. ( ⑤ ) Understanding which logic is at work can spare travelers and newcomers considerable embarrassment, and it may also explain why the same polite gesture can seem generous in one place and cold in another.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

In such settings, an immediate return of equal value can feel less like gratitude than like an attempt to close the account.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 such settings는 선물이 관계를 끝내지 않고 열어 두려는 곳(③ 앞 문장)을 가리키고, 주어진 문장에서 처음 나온 close the account를 ③ 뒤 문장이 And closing the account로 이어받아요. ②에 넣으면 빠른 답례를 기대하는 공동체 설명과 충돌해요.

items.passage: Researchers once trained a small group of guppies to swim to a feeding site by one of two routes through a tank. They then gradually removed the trained fish one at a time, replacing each with an untrained newcomer. The newcomers, simply by swimming along with the others, adopted the established route. Remarkably, even after every one of the original trained fish had been removed, the group continued to favor the same path, although the other route would have served just as well. In some trials, the trained fish had been taught a deliberately longer route, and this inefficient habit was passed on all the same, lasting far longer than one might expect. What persisted, then, was not the memory of any individual but a pattern carried by the group, renewed each time a newcomer copied those around it. The researchers concluded that such traditions need neither a teacher who understands the purpose of a behavior nor learners who weigh its advantages; simply following others can be enough to keep a custom alive.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

In groups of guppies, a route preference can be (A) ___ merely through copying, surviving the departure of all its original members even when the route is (B) ___.
items.exp: 새로 들어온 물고기들이 다른 물고기를 따라 헤엄치며 경로를 익혔으니 (A)는 transmitted(전달되는)이고, 일부러 더 긴 경로를 가르쳐도 그대로 전해졌으니 (B)는 inefficient(비효율적인)예요. 학습자가 장점을 따지지 않는다고 했으므로 evaluated는 맞지 않아요.

items.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, nutrition science advanced by isolating nutrients. Researchers identified vitamins, measured their effects one at a time, and assigned each food a value based on the sum of its components. This (a)[reductionist] approach produced real triumphs: it explained deficiency diseases such as scurvy and rickets and made fortified foods possible. Yet it rested on an assumption that is increasingly questioned—that a nutrient behaves the same way regardless of the food that delivers it.

Consider the fat in dairy products. If fat were simply fat, the saturated fat in cheese should affect blood cholesterol just as the same amount in butter does. Several controlled studies, however, have found that cheese tends to raise cholesterol (b)[less] than butter containing an equivalent quantity of fat. One explanation points to the structure of cheese itself: its calcium, its proteins, and the membranes surrounding its fat droplets appear to alter how much fat the gut absorbs. Similarly, the sugar in a whole apple enters the bloodstream more (c)[gradually] than the same sugar in apple juice, because intact cell walls slow its release during digestion.

Scientists now refer to this web of physical and chemical interactions as the 'food matrix.' The concept implies that two foods with identical nutrition labels may have quite (d)[different] effects on the body, and that grinding, heating, or refining a food can change its impact even when its nutrient content stays the same. It also complicates the design of supplements, since a vitamin extracted from its natural setting may not work as it did within the food.

None of this means that the study of individual nutrients was a mistake. It does suggest, however, that dietary advice built solely on counting components will remain (e)[complete] until it accounts for the way those components are packaged.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Beyond the Label: How the Package Shapes the Nutrient
Cheese or Butter? The Final Verdict on Dietary Fat
The Triumph of Vitamins over Deficiency Diseases
Why Supplements Work Better Than Whole Foods
Processing Food: A Simple Way to Boost Nutrition
items.exp: 같은 영양소라도 그것을 담은 식품의 구조(식품 매트릭스)에 따라 몸에 미치는 효과가 달라진다는 것이 글의 중심이에요. ②는 하나의 예시일 뿐이고, ④와 ⑤는 글 내용과 반대예요.

items.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, nutrition science advanced by isolating nutrients. Researchers identified vitamins, measured their effects one at a time, and assigned each food a value based on the sum of its components. This (a)[reductionist] approach produced real triumphs: it explained deficiency diseases such as scurvy and rickets and made fortified foods possible. Yet it rested on an assumption that is increasingly questioned—that a nutrient behaves the same way regardless of the food that delivers it.

Consider the fat in dairy products. If fat were simply fat, the saturated fat in cheese should affect blood cholesterol just as the same amount in butter does. Several controlled studies, however, have found that cheese tends to raise cholesterol (b)[less] than butter containing an equivalent quantity of fat. One explanation points to the structure of cheese itself: its calcium, its proteins, and the membranes surrounding its fat droplets appear to alter how much fat the gut absorbs. Similarly, the sugar in a whole apple enters the bloodstream more (c)[gradually] than the same sugar in apple juice, because intact cell walls slow its release during digestion.

Scientists now refer to this web of physical and chemical interactions as the 'food matrix.' The concept implies that two foods with identical nutrition labels may have quite (d)[different] effects on the body, and that grinding, heating, or refining a food can change its impact even when its nutrient content stays the same. It also complicates the design of supplements, since a vitamin extracted from its natural setting may not work as it did within the food.

None of this means that the study of individual nutrients was a mistake. It does suggest, however, that dietary advice built solely on counting components will remain (e)[complete] until it accounts for the way those components are packaged.
items.q: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 구성 성분만 세는 식단 조언은 성분이 담긴 방식을 고려하기 전까지 불완전할 것이라는 흐름이므로 (e) complete를 incomplete로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 영양소를 하나씩 분리하는 환원주의, 치즈가 콜레스테롤을 덜 올림, 당이 더 천천히 흡수됨, 서로 다른 효과로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Hana had not wanted to come. When her father announced that the family would spend the long weekend at Pine Hollow, a campsite two hours' drive from the nearest town, she had argued that she had a history project due and that there would be no signal in the mountains. Her father only smiled and packed an extra flashlight. Now, as the car bumped along the gravel road, Hana stared out the window at the endless trees and wondered how (a)[she] would survive three days without her friends' messages.

(B)
By the time the rain stopped, the sky was turning pale. Hana crawled out of the tent and found her father already crouched beside the fire pit, trying in vain to coax a flame from damp twigs. Without a word, (b)[she] fetched the bag of dry pine needles she had slid under the car the evening before, and soon a small fire was crackling between them. Her father looked at (c)[her] with open surprise. 'Where did you learn that?' he asked. 'From you,' she said. 'You were talking to Min-jun, but I was listening.'

(C)
The campsite sat beside a narrow stream. While her younger brother Min-jun chased frogs along the bank, Hana reluctantly helped her father raise the tent. He talked the whole time, explaining how to angle the stakes against the wind and why a tarp should hang lower on the side the weather comes from. As the sun set, he showed Min-jun how to stuff dry pine needles into a plastic bag and keep it somewhere sheltered. 'Wet wood will test your patience,' (d)[he] said, 'but dry tinder will save your pride.' Hana rolled her eyes, though she quietly filled a bag of her own and slid it under the car.

(D)
Around midnight, the wind rose and rain began drumming on the tent. Within minutes a cold trickle was running across the floor, and Min-jun began to cry. Remembering what she had heard that afternoon, Hana pulled on her raincoat, stepped out into the dark, and lowered the tarp on the windward side, tying it firmly to a tree with the knot (e)[she] had watched her father tie. The trickle stopped. Back inside, soaked but strangely calm, Hana wrapped her brother in a dry blanket and told him stories until he fell asleep.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 캠핑장에 도착해 아버지가 텐트 치는 법과 마른 불쏘시개 보관법을 알려 주는 (C), 그날 오후 들은 것을 떠올려 한밤중 폭우 속에서 방수포를 고쳐 묶는 (D), 비가 그친 새벽 전날 넣어 둔 솔잎으로 불을 피우는 (B) 순서예요. (D)의 'that afternoon'과 (B)의 'By the time the rain stopped'가 단서예요.

items.q: 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: Hana는 역사 과제가 있다며 캠핑을 반대했다.
Hana가 불을 피우자 아버지는 놀란 표정을 지었다.
Hana는 마른 솔잎을 담은 봉지를 차 밑에 넣어 두었다.
Hana는 한밤중에 방수포를 낮추어 나무에 묶었다.
items.exp: 아버지와 함께 텐트를 친 사람은 Hana이고, Min-jun은 그동안 개울가에서 개구리를 쫓아다녔어요. 나머지는 역사 과제, 아버지의 놀란 표정, 차 밑의 솔잎 봉지, 한밤중 방수포 내용과 일치해요.

items.passage:
Dear Mr. Hollis,

I am a resident of Fenwick Gardens and walk the Willow Creek trail most evenings, as do many of my neighbors. Since early October, five of the lamps along the stretch between the footbridge and the north gate have stopped working. After sunset that section is now almost completely dark, and the uneven paving stones there have already caused at least two falls that I know of, including one involving an elderly neighbor who injured her wrist. Several parents have also told me they no longer allow their teenagers to use the trail on their way home from evening classes. I reported the problem through the city's online form three weeks ago but have received only an automated reply. Some residents have even suggested organizing a volunteer patrol with flashlights, but that would hardly be a lasting solution. I would therefore be most grateful if your department could arrange for the broken lamps to be repaired as soon as possible, before the days grow even shorter.

Yours sincerely,
Grace Lindqvist
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 공원의 야간 개방 시간 연장을 요청하려고
산책로의 고장 난 가로등 수리를 요청하려고
온라인 민원 신청 방식의 개선을 건의하려고
items.exp: 산책로의 가로등 다섯 개가 고장 나 넘어지는 사고가 생기고 있으니 가능한 한 빨리 수리해 달라고 부탁하는 편지예요. 자원봉사 순찰대는 오래가는 해결책이 아니라고 했고, 온라인 신청은 이미 해 보았다는 사정 설명일 뿐이에요.

items.passage: For weeks I had circled the date on my calendar: the one night the comet would be at its brightest before slipping back into the dark for another seventy years. I drove my telescope two hours into the hills, set it up on a gravel turnout, and watched in disbelief as a thick bank of cloud rolled in from the west and swallowed the entire sky. I checked the satellite images on my phone again and again, as if staring at them could change what they showed. By midnight my hands were numb, my thermos was empty, and I was muttering at the sky like a man arguing with a referee. I had just begun to fold the tripod legs when I noticed that the gravel around me had brightened. A ragged gap was opening overhead, and there, framed by the torn edges of the cloud, hung the comet, its pale tail streaming across a quarter of the sky. I forgot the cold entirely. I stood there laughing, my eye pressed to the eyepiece, afraid to blink.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 I의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 기다리던 밤에 구름이 하늘을 덮어 휴대폰만 들여다보고 하늘에 대고 투덜댈 만큼 답답했어요. 구름 사이로 혜성이 나타나자 추위도 잊고 웃으며 바라보았으니 기쁨으로 바뀐 거예요.

items.passage: For decades, the standard answer to traffic congestion was to build more road space. If a highway was jammed at rush hour, engineers added a lane, and for a few months journeys did become quicker. Then the traffic returned, often heavier than before. Transport researchers now regard this pattern as one of the most reliable findings in their field. When driving becomes easier, people respond: some who had taken the train switch to their cars, others travel at peak times they once avoided, and new housing and shopping centers spring up along the widened route. The added capacity is soon filled by trips that would not otherwise have been made. Widening roads to cure congestion is, in this sense, rather like [loosening one's belt to cure overeating]. It relieves the immediate discomfort while encouraging the very behavior that produced it. Cities that have succeeded in reducing congestion have generally done the opposite, pricing road space, improving public transport, and making it easier to reach daily destinations without a car.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [loosening one's belt to cure overeating]이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: building new roads at the edge of a city rather than in its center
accommodating a problem in a way that invites more of it
ignoring warning signs until a problem becomes severe
cutting public spending in order to change people's habits
forcing drivers to give up their cars against their will
items.exp: 도로를 넓히면 당장은 막힘이 줄지만 더 많은 운전을 불러 다시 막히듯, 문제를 받아 주는 방식이 오히려 그 문제를 더 키운다는 뜻이에요. ③처럼 경고를 무시하는 것이 아니라 적극적으로 대응한 것이 역효과를 낸다는 점이 핵심이에요.

items.passage: When people describe how they feel, many rely on a small handful of words: good, bad, stressed, fine. Psychologists who study emotion have found that this vocabulary matters more than it might seem. Some individuals routinely distinguish between being disappointed, embarrassed, resentful, or lonely, whereas others lump all of these together as simply feeling 'bad.' Those who make finer distinctions tend to cope better with difficult experiences. They are less likely to drink heavily when upset, less likely to lash out at others, and quicker to recover from setbacks. One explanation is that a precise label carries information about what to do next. Knowing that one is lonely rather than merely unhappy points toward reaching out to a friend; recognizing irritation as the product of fatigue suggests rest rather than an argument. A vague feeling, by contrast, offers no direction and is easily mistaken for something else. Encouragingly, this skill appears to be learnable: people who practice describing their feelings in specific terms gradually become better at managing them.
items.q: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 감정을 억누르기보다 솔직하게 표현하는 것이 건강에 좋다.
부정적인 감정은 긍정적인 감정보다 오래 지속된다.
어휘력이 풍부한 사람이 타인의 감정을 더 잘 읽는다.
감정을 세밀하게 구별해 이름 붙이면 감정을 다스리는 데 도움이 된다.
감정 조절 능력은 어린 시절의 경험으로 결정된다.
items.exp: 감정을 세밀하게 구별하는 사람이 어려운 일에 더 잘 대처하고, 정확한 이름이 다음에 할 일을 알려 주며, 이 능력은 연습으로 기를 수 있다는 내용이에요. ③은 타인의 감정 읽기를 말하지 않았고, ⑤는 배울 수 있다는 지문 내용과 반대예요.

items.passage: Some species of bamboo behave in a way that has long puzzled botanists. For decades—in certain cases for more than a century—they grow without producing a single flower. Then, within the space of a year or two, every plant of the species across a vast region blooms at once, releases an enormous quantity of seeds, and dies. Such synchrony is costly, since a plant that waits so long risks being destroyed before it ever reproduces. One widely discussed explanation focuses on the animals that eat bamboo seeds. Rats, birds, and other seed predators can consume nearly all the seeds produced in an ordinary year, but they cannot possibly eat everything when an entire region floods them with food at the same moment. A fraction of the seeds survives simply because there are too many to be eaten. The long gaps between flowering events also prevent predator populations from adapting to a regular supply. By concentrating its reproduction into rare, overwhelming bursts, the plant turns the limited appetite of its enemies into an advantage.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the life cycle of bamboo used in traditional construction
ways in which rodents adapt to sudden food shortages
the effect of climate change on the flowering of plants
why bamboo spreads faster than other kinds of grass
a possible benefit of plants flowering all at once at long intervals
items.exp: 대나무가 오랜 간격을 두고 한꺼번에 꽃을 피우면 씨앗을 먹는 동물이 다 먹지 못해 일부 씨앗이 살아남는다는, 동시 개화의 이점을 설명하는 글이에요. ②는 쥐가 적응하지 못하게 한다는 내용과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: Airlines routinely sell more tickets for a flight than there are seats on the plane. To many travelers this practice seems close to dishonest, but it rests on a simple statistical observation: on almost every flight, some passengers who have bought tickets do not show up. They miss connections, fall ill, or change their plans, and on many routes their tickets can be refunded or exchanged. An aircraft that departs with empty seats has lost revenue it can never recover, since a seat cannot be stored and sold the following week. By studying years of records, airlines can estimate fairly precisely how many passengers are likely to be absent on a given route, day, and season, and they sell roughly that many extra tickets. The bet does not always pay off. When more passengers appear than expected, the airline must persuade some to take a later flight, usually by offering cash or travel vouchers. Yet because such cases are relatively rare, the money gained from fuller flights generally far exceeds the cost of compensation.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Hidden Dangers of Overcrowded Flights
How Passengers Can Avoid Paying for Missed Flights
Selling Seats That Don't Exist: A Bet on Absent Passengers
Why Refundable Tickets Cost More Than Others
Airline Vouchers: A Reward for Loyal Customers
items.exp: 항공사가 결석할 승객 수를 통계로 예측해 좌석보다 많은 표를 팔고, 가끔 보상 비용이 들어도 그 이익이 더 크다는 내용이므로 ③이 가장 알맞아요. ⑤의 바우처는 초과 예약이 빗나갔을 때의 보상 수단일 뿐이에요.

items.passage:
Greenfield Seed Swap 2027

Bring the seeds you have saved and take home something new! Our annual swap connects home gardeners across the county.

• When: Saturday, March 13, 2027, 10 a.m. – 2 p.m.
• Where: Greenfield Public Library, Community Hall (2nd floor)
• Admission: Free for everyone
• Seed packets: Bring up to 10 packets to trade. No seeds? You may still take up to 3 packets for a donation of $1 each.

Activities
• 10:30 a.m. Workshop: Saving Tomato Seeds (limited to 25 people, sign up at the front desk on the day)
• 12:30 p.m. Talk: Planning a Small Vegetable Garden

Notes
• Please label each packet with the plant name and the year it was collected.
• Seeds from invasive plant species will not be accepted.
• Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.
items.q: Greenfield Seed Swap 2027에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 씨앗을 가져오지 않은 사람은 참여할 수 없다.
토마토 씨앗 받기 워크숍은 25명으로 인원이 제한된다.
씨앗 봉투에 식물 이름과 채집 연도를 적어야 한다.
12세 미만 어린이는 어른과 함께 와야 한다.
items.exp: 씨앗이 없는 사람도 봉투당 1달러를 기부하면 3봉투까지 가져갈 수 있다고 했으므로 ②가 일치하지 않아요. 나머지는 장소, 워크숍 인원 제한, 봉투 표기, 어린이 동반 안내와 일치해요.

items.passage: A fever is often treated as an enemy to be defeated as quickly as possible, yet in many cases it forms part of the body's defense. When the immune system detects an infection, chemical signals travel to the hypothalamus, the region of the brain that ①[acts] as the body's thermostat, and its set point is raised by a degree or two. The resulting rise in temperature slows the reproduction of many bacteria and viruses, ②[which] multiply most efficiently at normal body temperature, while speeding up the activity of certain immune cells. Animal experiments point in the same direction: infected lizards kept at lower temperatures ③[were] more likely to die than those allowed to warm themselves. None of this means that a fever should never be reduced. A very high temperature can be dangerous, and medication can make a patient ④[to feel] comfortable enough to rest and drink fluids. But for an otherwise healthy adult with a moderate fever, many doctors now advise ⑤[treating] the person's discomfort rather than chasing a normal reading on the thermometer.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: 사역동사 make는 목적격 보어로 원형부정사를 쓰므로 to feel을 feel로 고쳐야 해요. ①은 단수 the region을 받는 동사, ②는 bacteria and viruses를 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사, ③은 복수 주어 lizards에 맞는 과거 동사, ⑤는 advise의 목적어인 동명사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Studies of waiting lines suggest that people's frustration depends less on how long they wait than on whether the wait seems fair. A single line feeding several counters is not necessarily faster on average than a separate line for each counter, yet customers tend to ①[prefer] it, because it guarantees that no one who arrives later will be served sooner. In separate lines, by contrast, watching a neighboring line move faster produces a sense of ②[injustice] out of proportion to the minutes actually lost. Uncertainty matters as well. A wait of unknown length feels ③[longer] than an equally long wait announced in advance, which is why many amusement parks post estimated times at the entrance to each ride and, it is said, sometimes deliberately ④[overstate] them so that visitors are pleasantly surprised. Finally, occupied time passes more quickly than empty time. Mirrors beside elevators and screens in waiting rooms ⑤[lengthen] the perceived wait by giving people something to attend to, which is why such simple devices have spread so widely.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 무언가에 신경을 쏟는 시간은 더 빨리 지나가므로 거울이나 화면은 체감 대기 시간을 줄여 줘요. 그래서 lengthen을 shorten으로 바꿔야 해요. ④는 방문객이 기분 좋게 놀라도록 일부러 '부풀려' 알린다는 뜻으로 맞아요.

items.passage: Before the invention of printing, every book had to be copied by hand, and every copy introduced new mistakes. A tired scribe might skip a line whose last word matched that of the line above, misread an unfamiliar term, or 'correct' a passage he did not understand. Over centuries, the surviving manuscripts of an ancient text came to differ from one another in thousands of small ways, and the original was lost. Remarkably, scholars have learned to work backward from this confusion. If several manuscripts share the same unusual error, they almost certainly descend from a common ancestor in which that error first appeared, while a manuscript lacking it must belong to a separate branch. By tracing such shared slips, researchers can build a kind of family tree of copies and, by comparing its independent branches, infer what the lost original most probably said. In this way, the very mistakes that corrupted the text become ___ for recovering it, and a careless scribe of the ninth century may unknowingly help a modern editor.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 여러 사본이 공유하는 오류를 추적해 사본의 계보를 세우고 원문을 추론하므로, 원문을 훼손한 실수가 오히려 원문을 되찾는 '단서'가 돼요. obstacles는 오류가 복원을 돕는다는 글의 핵심과 반대예요.

items.passage: We tend to judge democracies by their winners: by the parties that take office and the policies they enact. Yet the survival of democratic government depends at least as much on its losers. Every election leaves a large share of citizens, sometimes nearly half, governed by people they voted against, and nothing in the counting of ballots compels them to accept the result. That they usually do so peacefully is easy to take for granted. Political scientists who study this 'losers' consent' have found that it is not grounded mainly in agreement. Defeated voters rarely come to believe that the winners were right, and in bitterly divided societies they may regard their opponents' values with open hostility. What sustains their acceptance appears instead to be a judgment about the process. Where losers trust that elections will continue to be held, counted honestly, and decided under rules that do not tilt permanently toward those in power, they can afford to wait. Their consent, in other words, rests less on approval of the present outcome than on confidence that ___. Where that confidence collapses, the losing side has far less reason to accept defeat.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the winning side truly represents the will of the majority
their opponents will come to share their basic political values
the rules will leave them a fair chance to win in the future
public protest will eventually reverse the result of the election
the economy will continue to grow regardless of who governs
items.exp: 패자가 결과를 받아들이는 근거는 승자에 대한 동의가 아니라, 선거가 계속 공정하게 치러지고 규칙이 권력자 쪽으로 영구히 기울지 않는다는 믿음이므로 다음에 이길 공정한 기회가 남아 있다는 확신이에요. ①과 ②는 동의나 가치 공유에 근거하지 않는다는 지문 내용과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: When a large whale dies in the open ocean, its body often sinks to the deep seafloor, where food is normally extremely scarce, and becomes the basis of a temporary community that may last for decades. ① In the first months, scavengers such as hagfish and sleeper sharks gather in large numbers to strip away the soft tissue, consuming many tonnes of flesh. ② Living whales also enrich the ocean by releasing nutrient-rich waste near the surface, where it fertilizes the plankton at the base of the food web. ③ Once the flesh is gone, worms, snails, and small crustaceans colonize the exposed bones and the surrounding sediment, feeding on the remaining scraps and organic matter. ④ Later still, bacteria break down the fats stored inside the bones, releasing chemical compounds that support yet another set of organisms. ⑤ Some of the species found at these sites have been discovered nowhere else, suggesting that they depend on a chain of such carcasses scattered across the ocean floor to complete their life cycles.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 글은 죽은 고래가 심해저에 가라앉은 뒤 청소 동물, 뼈를 차지하는 생물, 박테리아 순으로 이어지는 공동체를 다루어요. ②는 살아 있는 고래가 바다 표층을 비옥하게 한다는 내용이라 사체 생태계의 단계 설명에서 벗어나요.

items.passage:
Every flat map of the world is a compromise. The surface of a sphere cannot be spread onto a plane without being stretched, squeezed, or torn somewhere, so mapmakers must decide which properties to keep accurate and which to sacrifice.

(A) That property made the map invaluable to sailors, who could plot a course across an ocean with nothing more than a ruler and a compass. The price, however, was paid in area: to keep angles true, the map enlarges regions more and more as they approach the poles.

(B) As a result, Greenland appears roughly as large as Africa, although Africa is in fact about fourteen times bigger. Because the map has hung for generations in classrooms, such distortions have shaped many people's mental picture of the world.

(C) The projection published by Gerardus Mercator in 1569 made a particular choice. It preserved angles, so that a line of constant compass direction appears on the map as a straight line.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 무엇을 지킬지 골라야 한다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 메르카토르 도법이 각도를 지켰다는 (C)가 오고, (A)의 That property가 그 각도 보존을 받아요. (A) 끝의 극지방 확대를 As a result로 받아 그린란드 예를 드는 (B)가 마지막이에요.

items.passage: Supporters of remote work point to its obvious benefits: no commute, fewer interruptions, and greater freedom to arrange the working day. ( ① ) Studies of productivity often confirm that people working from home complete as many tasks as those in the office, if not more. ( ② ) What such studies measure less easily, however, is the knowledge that passes between colleagues without anyone intending to pass it on. ( ③ ) In an office, a junior employee overhears how a senior colleague calms an angry client, or learns from a chance conversation in the hallway which manager to approach with a particular problem. ( ④ ) Remote tools leave a gap here, because such encounters cannot be scheduled; nobody books a video call to ask a question they do not yet know they have. ( ⑤ ) For this reason, some firms that otherwise allow flexible arrangements ask new hires to spend their first months working alongside colleagues in person, so that this informal learning has a chance to take place.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

This gap falls hardest on newcomers, who have the most to learn and the fewest people they feel free to ask.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 This gap은 ⑤ 앞 문장의 '원격 도구가 남기는 공백'을 가리키고, 주어진 문장의 newcomers를 ⑤ 뒤 문장이 For this reason으로 받아 신입 사원의 출근 이야기로 이어져요. 다른 자리에는 This gap이 가리킬 대상이 없어요.

items.passage: When a weather forecast announces a '30 percent chance of rain,' most people pay attention, but they do not all hear the same message. In surveys conducted in several cities, some respondents took the figure to mean that it would rain over 30 percent of the region, others that it would rain for 30 percent of the day, and still others that 30 percent of forecasters expected rain. Meteorologists intend something different: on days with conditions like these, rain falls at a given location on roughly three days out of ten. The number itself is not the source of the confusion. What the statement leaves out is the answer to a simple question—30 percent of what? Without being told whether the figure refers to areas, hours, or days, listeners fill the gap with whatever interpretation comes to mind first, and people in the same household may make quite different plans from the same broadcast. Researchers have therefore suggested that forecasters state explicitly what kind of event the percentage describes.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

A probability forecast is often (A) ___ by the public, mainly because it leaves unstated the class of events to which the number (B) ___.
items.exp: 사람들이 같은 '30퍼센트'를 지역, 시간, 예보관 비율 등으로 제각각 이해하므로 (A)는 misinterpreted(잘못 해석되는)이고, 그 숫자가 무엇에 대한 것인지를 말하지 않는 것이 원인이므로 (B)는 applies(적용되는)예요. 대부분 주의를 기울인다고 했으니 ignored는 맞지 않아요.

items.passage:
It is often said that a scientific theory is tested by deriving a prediction from it and checking whether the prediction comes true; if it fails, the theory should be abandoned. The history of science shows that matters are rarely so (a)[simple]. A prediction never follows from a theory alone. It also depends on auxiliary assumptions about instruments, initial conditions, and the absence of interfering factors. When an observation conflicts with a prediction, logic tells us only that something in this whole bundle is wrong, not which part.

In the 1840s, astronomers noticed that Uranus was not moving quite as Newton's theory of gravitation predicted. Rather than (b)[accepting] Newton's laws, the French astronomer Urbain Le Verrier assumed that an unseen planet was pulling Uranus off course and calculated where it must be. In 1846 Neptune was found close to the predicted position. The theory had been (c)[rescued] by questioning an auxiliary assumption, namely that no other planet lay beyond Uranus.

Encouraged, Le Verrier later applied the same strategy to Mercury, whose orbit also showed a small irregularity. He proposed another hidden planet, soon called Vulcan, circling close to the Sun. Despite years of searching, no such planet was ever (d)[confirmed]. The irregularity was finally explained in 1915 by Einstein's general theory of relativity, which replaced Newton's account rather than repairing it.

The two episodes relied on the same reasoning, yet one ended in triumph and the other in failure. This suggests that no rule of logic can tell scientists in advance whether to defend a theory or give it up. The decision requires (e)[judgment]: about how well supported the theory already is, how plausible the rescuing assumption seems, and whether that assumption leads to new predictions that can themselves be tested.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Newton's Errors: How Einstein Corrected Classical Physics
The Search for Vulcan: A Forgotten Planet
Why Scientific Predictions Are Always Reliable
When a Prediction Fails, What Exactly Has Failed?
Hidden Planets and the Limits of Early Telescopes
items.exp: 예측이 빗나가도 이론 자체가 틀렸는지 보조 가정이 틀렸는지 논리만으로는 알 수 없다는 점을 해왕성과 불칸의 사례로 보여 주는 글이에요. ①과 ②는 사례의 일부만 다루고, ③은 글 내용과 반대예요.

items.exp: Le Verrier는 뉴턴의 법칙을 버리는 대신 보이지 않는 행성을 가정했으므로 (b) accepting을 abandoning으로 바꿔야 해요. 나머지는 일이 그렇게 단순하지 않음, 이론이 구출됨, 행성이 확인되지 않음, 판단이 필요함으로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Theo had lived his whole life in a town where everyone knew his name. Then his mother accepted a job in the city, and in the space of a single week he found himself on the ninth floor of an apartment building where neighbors nodded in the elevator and looked away. At his new school, nobody was unkind, but nobody seemed to notice him either. In the evenings (a)[he] sat by the window, watching thousands of lit windows across the street and feeling more invisible than ever.

(B)
Over the following weeks, Mr. Barlow taught him the names of every bird and explained how homing pigeons work. 'You can take one a hundred kilometers away,' he said, 'and it'll fly straight back here. Nobody's sure exactly how. But it has to live somewhere a while before it knows that's home.' Theo thought about that for a long time. Then one icy morning, Mr. Barlow slipped on the stairs and hurt his knee. From his armchair, (b)[he] handed over the key to the roof. 'They'll need feeding twice a day,' he said, and (c)[the boy] nodded, trying not to look as proud as he felt.

(C)
While the old man's knee healed, Theo cared for the birds every morning and evening. One afternoon he carried a pigeon to school in a ventilated box, and at lunch a group of classmates gathered around, asking questions he could finally answer. A girl named Priya helped (d)[him] release the bird on the playing field. They watched it circle twice and head east. When Theo got home, the pigeon was already waiting on the roof, and he realized, with some surprise, that he had been thinking of the building as home all the way there.

(D)
One Saturday, a soft cooing drifted through the ceiling. Curious, Theo climbed the service stairs and pushed open the door to the roof. There, among potted tomatoes and a wooden coop, stood an elderly man in a faded cap. 'Close that door, you'll let the cold in,' the man grumbled, without looking up. Then he pushed a bag of seed into Theo's hands. 'Name's Barlow. Since you're here, make yourself useful.' Theo stayed for an hour, and the next day (e)[he] came back without being asked.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 외로워하던 Theo가 옥상에서 비둘기를 키우는 노인을 처음 만나는 (D), 그 뒤 몇 주 동안 Mr. Barlow에게 배우다가 노인이 다쳐 옥상 열쇠를 받는 (B), 노인의 무릎이 낫는 동안 비둘기를 돌보며 친구를 사귀는 (C) 순서예요. (B)의 Over the following weeks와 (C)의 While the old man's knee healed가 단서예요.

items.passage:
Dear Members of the Library Board,

I am writing on behalf of the Student Council of Westbrook High School, which serves roughly nine hundred students in the eastern district. For many of our students, the second-floor study room at Westbrook Public Library is not merely a convenient place to work; it is the only quiet space available to them. A considerable number live in crowded apartments where sharing a single room with younger siblings makes sustained concentration nearly impossible. At present, the study room closes at 7 p.m., which leaves students with barely two hours after classes end. During the final examination period, from June 14 to June 30, this constraint becomes especially burdensome. We therefore respectfully ask that the board consider keeping the study room open until 10 p.m. throughout those two weeks. Our council has already recruited twelve parent volunteers who are willing to help supervise the room in the evenings, so the additional burden on library staff would be minimal. We would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss this proposal at your next meeting.

Sincerely,
Daniel Moon
President, Westbrook High School Student Council
items.q: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 시험 기간 동안 자습실 운영 시간 연장을 요청하려고
도서관 이사회 회의 일정 변경을 알리려고
학생회 주최 학습 프로그램의 장소 대여를 문의하려고
items.exp: 기말고사 기간인 6월 14일부터 30일까지 자습실을 오후 10시까지 열어 달라고 정중히 요청하고 있어요. 학부모 자원봉사자 이야기는 요청을 뒷받침하는 근거일 뿐 감사나 모집이 목적은 아니에요.

items.passage: The fog came down faster than Hana had thought possible. One moment the ridge stretched before her in clear autumn light; the next, the trail markers dissolved into a gray wall, and even her own boots seemed to blur at the edges. She stopped, her heart pounding, and pulled out her phone only to find that the signal bar had vanished. Every direction looked identical. She tried to recall whether the last fork had bent left or right, but her memory offered nothing but a confused tangle of rocks and roots. Her breath grew shallow, and she pressed her back against a cold boulder, telling herself not to move. Then, faintly, she heard it: the hollow clank of a bell. It was the bell that hung at the mountain shelter, the one hikers rang for luck. Following the sound step by careful step, she soon made out the dark outline of the shelter's roof. When her hand finally touched its wooden door, the tightness in her chest loosened, and she laughed out loud at nothing in particular, grateful simply to know where she was.
items.q: 다음 글에 드러난 Hana의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 안개 속에서 길을 잃고 심장이 뛰며 숨이 가빠지다가, 종소리를 따라 대피소 문에 손이 닿자 가슴의 긴장이 풀리고 웃음이 났어요. 그래서 anxious → relieved가 알맞아요.

items.passage: Every autumn, homeowners and city crews spend enormous amounts of time and fuel removing fallen leaves from lawns, parks, and roadside strips, bagging them, and trucking them to distant landfills. The habit feels like responsible maintenance, yet it quietly undermines the very ecosystems it claims to tidy. A layer of leaves is not litter; it is a winter shelter for countless insects, including the larvae of many moths and butterflies that birds depend on in spring. As the leaves decompose, they return nitrogen and carbon to the soil, reducing the need for the chemical fertilizers that are later purchased to replace exactly what was hauled away. Meanwhile, leaves sealed in plastic bags decay without oxygen in landfills and release methane, a potent greenhouse gas. None of this means that every sidewalk must be buried. Leaves that block drains or cover paths should certainly be cleared. But in garden beds, under trees, and along the edges of parks, we should let fallen leaves stay where they land, treating them as a resource to be kept rather than a mess to be removed.
items.q: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 낙엽을 비료로 가공하는 시설을 확충해야 한다.
낙엽을 수거할 때 비닐봉지 대신 종이봉투를 사용해야 한다.
곤충 보호를 위해 정원에서 화학 비료 사용을 금지해야 한다.
화단이나 공원 가장자리의 낙엽은 치우지 말고 그대로 두어야 한다.
items.exp: 마지막 문장에서 화단, 나무 아래, 공원 가장자리의 낙엽은 떨어진 자리에 그대로 두고 자원으로 여기자고 주장해요. 배수구를 막는 낙엽은 치워야 한다는 말은 예외를 인정한 것일 뿐 주장이 아니에요.

items.passage: Scientists are trained to separate signal from noise. A measurement that falls far from the expected value is often treated as an error, such as a loose cable, a contaminated sample, or a careless reading, and quietly removed so that the clean pattern can emerge. Much of the time this is sensible; instruments do fail, and not every oddity deserves a paper. Yet the history of science suggests that some of its most important turns began precisely with results that refused to fit. A faint, persistent hiss in a radio antenna and a photographic plate fogged where no light should have reached it were at first dismissed as nuisances before they were recognized as evidence of something no theory had anticipated. The difficulty is that anomalies do not announce their importance. They look exactly like mistakes until someone takes the trouble to rule out every ordinary explanation. A researcher who develops the habit of [listening to the noise in the instrument] therefore accepts a slower, less tidy path, but it is often the only path that leads beyond what is already known.
items.q: 밑줄 친 [listening to the noise in the instrument]가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: taking seemingly faulty data seriously as a possible sign of the unknown
repairing measuring devices before conducting further experiments
ignoring minor errors so that the main pattern becomes clear
relying on the judgment of colleagues rather than on instruments
repeating the same experiment until the results match the theory
items.exp: 기대에서 벗어난 측정값은 오류처럼 보이지만, 그런 이상 결과가 과학의 중요한 전환점이 되기도 했다고 했어요. 따라서 밑줄은 오류처럼 보이는 자료를 미지의 신호일 수 있다고 진지하게 다루는 태도예요. ③은 글에서 말하는 일반적 관행으로, 밑줄과 반대예요.

items.passage: To an observer, the sloth's slowness looks like a flaw, the mark of an animal that barely seems to try. In fact, its sluggishness is a finely balanced solution to a difficult diet. Sloths feed mainly on leaves, which are low in calories, hard to digest, and often laced with mild toxins. Digesting such food takes time; a single meal may remain in a sloth's multi-chambered stomach for weeks. Rather than search for more food, the sloth reduces what it spends. Its metabolic rate is among the lowest of any mammal its size, and its muscle mass is far smaller than that of comparable tree-dwelling animals, cutting the energy needed simply to stay alive. Even its body temperature is allowed to drift with the surrounding air, so it does not burn fuel to keep warm; instead, it basks in the sun. Its slow movements serve a second purpose as well: predators such as eagles, which locate prey largely by detecting motion, often overlook a creature that hardly moves at all. What appears to be laziness is thus an economy of energy shaped by the leaves it eats.
items.q: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: the harmful effects of leaf toxins on tree-dwelling mammals
reasons predators prefer slow-moving prey in the rainforest
slowness as an energy-saving adaptation to a poor diet
the role of sunlight in the digestion of plant material
differences in muscle structure among large mammals
items.exp: 나무늘보의 느림은 열량이 낮은 잎을 먹는 데 맞춘 에너지 절약 방식이라는 내용이에요. 낮은 대사율, 적은 근육량, 체온 조절 생략이 모두 그 근거예요. ②는 오히려 포식자가 움직이지 않는 먹이를 놓친다는 내용과 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: It is natural to assume that secondhand markets compete with manufacturers, stealing sales whenever a buyer chooses a used bicycle or a pre-owned camera over a new one. Economists have found the relationship to be more cooperative than it appears. When a product can be resold easily, its first buyer is not really paying the full sticker price; part of that price will later be recovered from the next owner. A buyer who expects to sell a jacket for half its original cost after two years is effectively renting it for the other half, and this lower effective cost makes the initial purchase easier to justify. Active resale markets therefore tend to raise people's willingness to pay for new goods, particularly durable items that hold their value. They also shift buyers toward higher-quality products, because a well-made item retains more of its price when resold. Some brands have recognized this and now operate their own resale programs, treating a product's second life not as a threat but as part of its appeal on the day it is first sold.
items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Used Goods Are Always Cheaper Than New Ones
Manufacturers Versus Resellers: A Battle for Buyers
How Renting Replaced Ownership in Modern Markets
A Second Life That Sells the First: Resale and New Demand
The Hidden Costs of Buying Pre-Owned Products
items.exp: 되팔 수 있으면 첫 구매의 실질 비용이 낮아져 새 제품을 사려는 의향이 커진다는 내용이에요. 그래서 중고 시장이 신제품 수요를 키운다는 ④가 알맞아요. ②는 글이 부정하는 통념이에요.

items.passage: Ilse Brandvold (1874–1951) was a Norwegian mapmaker whose charts of the country's northern coastline remained in use for half a century. The daughter of a lighthouse keeper, she spent her childhood on a rocky island where, from an early age, she sketched the outlines of the surrounding inlets in the margins of her father's logbooks. Because women were not admitted to the national surveying school at the time, she learned trigonometry from borrowed textbooks and practiced by measuring the distances between fishing villages on foot. In 1902, a set of coastal sketches she had mailed to a naval officer impressed him so much that he arranged for her to join a government survey ship as an assistant. Over the next twenty years, she personally charted more than three thousand kilometers of shoreline, often working from small open boats in freezing weather. Her maps were praised for marking underwater rocks that earlier charts had missed, and fishermen credited them with preventing countless wrecks. After retiring, she trained young surveyors and wrote a handbook on coastal measurement that was translated into four languages.
items.q: 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: 어린 시절 아버지의 업무 일지 여백에 섬 주변 해안선을 그렸다.
국립 측량 학교에 입학하여 삼각법을 정식으로 배웠다.
해군 장교의 주선으로 정부 측량선에 조수로 합류했다.
이전 해도들이 놓친 수중 암초를 표시해 호평을 받았다.
은퇴 후 젊은 측량사들을 가르치고 안내서를 집필했다.
items.exp: 당시 여성은 국립 측량 학교에 입학할 수 없어서 빌린 교과서로 삼각법을 혼자 배웠다고 했어요. 그래서 ②가 일치하지 않아요.

items.passage: When a regional dialect disappears, what is lost is more than a collection of quaint words. Dialects often preserve distinctions that the standard language has abandoned, ①[allowing] speakers to express shades of meaning that are otherwise difficult to capture. A farming community's dialect, for instance, might have separate words for snow that falls at night and snow ②[that] drifts against a wall, reflecting the close attention its members once had to pay to the weather. Linguists who record elderly speakers frequently find that such terms are known only to people over seventy, and that their grandchildren, ③[raised] on television and schooling in the standard form, recognize few of them. The decline is rarely the result of open suppression. More often, parents themselves choose to speak the standard variety at home, believing it ④[will offer] their children better opportunities. The process is quiet and voluntary, which is precisely why it is so hard to reverse: by the time a community notices ⑤[what] its dialect has become rare, few fluent speakers remain to teach it.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
items.exp: notices 뒤에는 완전한 절(its dialect has become rare)이 이어지므로 의문사 what이 아니라 접속사 that이 와야 해요. ①은 분사구문, ②는 snow를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사, ③은 grandchildren을 꾸미는 과거분사, ④는 believing의 목적어절 동사로 모두 맞아요.

items.passage: Endurance athletes preparing for a major race often receive a counterintuitive instruction from their coaches: in the final two weeks, train less. This practice, known as tapering, can feel deeply uncomfortable to athletes who have spent months believing that more work always produces better results. Yet hard training does not make the body stronger by itself; it creates small amounts of damage and fatigue, and the actual gains occur during the ①[recovery] that follows. When training load is sharply reduced before competition, the muscles finally have time to repair, energy stores are refilled, and the accumulated tiredness that has been ②[masking] the athlete's true fitness fades away. Studies of swimmers and runners have found that a well-planned taper can ③[lower] performance by several percent, a margin that often separates winners from the rest. The key is that intensity is ④[maintained] while volume falls; athletes still perform short, fast efforts so that their bodies do not lose sharpness. Many athletes report feeling restless during this period, but those who trust the process usually discover that rest, properly timed, is not a ⑤[break] from training but one of its most productive phases.
items.q: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 테이퍼링으로 피로가 사라지면 경기력이 좋아지고, 그 차이가 승자를 가른다고 했으므로 lower가 아니라 improve(또는 boost)가 되어야 해요. 나머지는 회복, 체력을 가리던 피로, 유지되는 강도, 훈련으로부터의 쉼이라는 흐름에 맞아요.

items.passage: Which do people regret more: the things they did or the things they failed to do? In the short term, actions tend to sting more sharply. A rash remark or an unwise purchase produces an immediate, vivid sense of having caused a bad outcome. Over longer stretches of time, however, the pattern reverses, and people looking back on their lives mention missed opportunities far more often than mistakes. One reason is that regrets of action tend to be repaired or reinterpreted; we apologize, learn a lesson, or tell ourselves the experience made us wiser. Regrets of inaction offer no such closure. Because the path not taken was never tested against reality, it remains open in the imagination, where it can grow endlessly more attractive. The job we did not apply for keeps getting better each year, untouched by the disappointments that a real job would have brought. In this sense, the pain of inaction lies in its ___: it can never be proven wrong, and so it never stops suggesting what might have been.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 하지 않은 일은 현실에서 검증된 적이 없어 상상 속에서 끝나지 않고 열린 채 남는다고 했어요. 그래서 끝맺어지지 않음, 즉 incompleteness가 알맞아요. suddenness는 단기적으로 더 아픈 행동의 후회에 해당해요.

items.passage: We tend to notice the systems that support daily life only at the moment they stop working. Few people think about water pressure, the timing of traffic signals, or the shared formats that let one computer read a file made on another, until a pipe bursts, an intersection jams, or a document arrives as a page of meaningless symbols. This is not simple carelessness. Infrastructure succeeds, in a sense, by disappearing; its purpose is to let attention flow toward other tasks, and a system that constantly demanded notice would be failing at its job. The consequence, however, is a peculiar political problem. Because well-functioning infrastructure generates no complaints, it also generates little support for its maintenance, and budgets for repair are easily cut in favor of projects that can be seen and celebrated. Decay accumulates silently beneath the surface of normal life. The very quality that makes such systems valuable thus ___, ensuring that the public discovers their worth chiefly through the experience of their collapse.
items.q: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: encourages citizens to demand constant improvements in their design
makes them easier to replace with newer and more visible projects
allows engineers to repair them without the public's knowledge
deprives them of the attention required to sustain them
forces governments to explain their technical details to voters
items.exp: 기반 시설은 눈에 띄지 않아야 제 역할을 하는데, 바로 그 때문에 불평도 지지도 생기지 않아 유지 예산이 깎인다고 했어요. 따라서 가치를 만드는 성질이 유지에 필요한 관심을 빼앗는다는 ④가 알맞아요. ②는 예산이 눈에 띄는 사업으로 간다는 말을 빌렸지만 시설을 대체한다는 내용은 없어요.

items.passage: Regular exercise has long been viewed as the main remedy for the health risks of modern sedentary life, but a growing body of research suggests that the problem cannot be solved by a single workout alone. ① A person who runs for forty minutes each morning and then sits almost motionless for the next ten hours may still face elevated risks of heart disease and metabolic disorders. ② Long, uninterrupted periods of sitting appear to slow the processes by which muscles absorb sugar and fat from the blood, and these effects are not fully reversed by a burst of activity earlier in the day. ③ Running, in particular, has become popular because it requires little equipment and can be done almost anywhere. ④ Encouragingly, the same studies indicate that breaking up sitting time with brief movement, such as standing to stretch or walking for two or three minutes every half hour, can noticeably improve how the body handles blood sugar. ⑤ The lesson, then, is that health depends not only on how much we exercise but also on how often we interrupt stillness throughout the day.
items.q: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
items.exp: 글은 운동만으로는 오래 앉아 있는 해로움을 없앨 수 없고 앉은 시간을 자주 끊어야 한다는 내용이에요. ③은 달리기가 인기 있는 이유를 말해 흐름에서 벗어나요.

items.passage:
Before refrigeration, preserving food through the long months of winter or the dry season was a matter of survival, and fermentation was among the most widespread solutions.

(A) By encouraging the growth of certain microbes, people could keep vegetables, milk, and fish edible for months, since these organisms produced acids and other compounds that kept harmful bacteria from multiplying. Cabbage packed with salt, milk left to sour in skin bags, and fish buried in clay pots all relied on this same invisible partnership.

(B) Over generations, these flavors became bound up with identity itself. A particular fermented paste or pickled vegetable came to signal home, family, and belonging, which is why such foods often survive long after refrigerators have made them unnecessary for preservation.

(C) Yet the methods that began as practical necessities did not remain merely practical. Because each region depended on its own local ingredients, climate, and microbial populations, the resulting foods developed strikingly distinct flavors, so that two villages only a valley apart might produce pickles that tasted nothing alike.
items.q: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 발효가 해결책이었다는 주어진 글 뒤에 미생물로 음식을 보존한 방법을 설명하는 (A)가 와요. (C)의 the methods that began as practical necessities가 (A)의 방법을 받고, (B)의 these flavors가 (C)의 distinct flavors를 받아요.

items.passage: The Moon's gravity does more than raise the tides; over immense spans of time, it is also gradually lengthening the day on Earth. ( ① ) As the Moon pulls on the oceans, it creates bulges of water, and as Earth rotates beneath them, these enormous masses of water rub against the seafloor and coastlines, losing energy as friction. ( ② ) The effect is tiny on a human scale, adding roughly two thousandths of a second to the length of a day every century. ( ③ ) Over geological time, however, it adds up dramatically: evidence preserved in the growth layers of ancient corals suggests that about 400 million years ago, a year contained more than 400 days, each considerably shorter than today's. ( ④ ) The energy that Earth loses does not simply vanish. ( ⑤ ) Part of it is transferred to the Moon, which is slowly spiraling outward, moving about four centimeters farther from Earth each year, a distance that scientists can measure precisely by bouncing laser beams off mirrors left on its surface.
items.q:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

This friction acts as a gentle brake on the planet's spin, slowing it down little by little.
items.exp: 주어진 문장의 This friction은 바로 앞 문장의 friction을 받고, 자전이 느려진다는 내용은 뒤 문장의 The effect(하루가 길어지는 효과)로 이어져요. ① 앞에는 아직 마찰이 나오지 않았고, ③ 이후는 이미 효과를 설명한 뒤라 어색해요.

items.passage: News organizations have traditionally been reluctant to publish corrections prominently, fearing that admitting mistakes will damage their credibility. Many have tucked corrections into small boxes on back pages or quietly edited online articles without noting the change. Research on audience reactions, however, points in the opposite direction. In a series of experiments, readers were shown news stories that contained an error, followed either by a clear, visible correction or by no correction at all. Those who saw the correction rated the outlet as more trustworthy overall, not less, and they were more likely to say they would return to it for future news. The researchers suggest that readers already assume journalists sometimes make errors; what they cannot see is whether an organization takes those errors seriously. A visible correction provides that evidence. By contrast, silently altered articles, when discovered, tended to provoke strong suspicion, as readers began to wonder what else had been changed without notice. Openly acknowledging mistakes, in other words, signals the very commitment to accuracy that hiding them is meant to protect.
items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Contrary to what news organizations fear, (A) ___ disclosure of their errors tends to (B) ___ readers' trust, because it shows that they take accuracy seriously.
items.exp: 눈에 띄게 정정한 기사를 본 독자가 언론사를 더 신뢰했다고 했어요. 그래서 (A)에는 공개적인 정정을 뜻하는 transparent, (B)에는 신뢰를 높인다는 reinforce가 와요. 조용히 고친 기사는 오히려 의심을 샀으므로 quiet는 맞지 않아요.

items.passage: When we stand before an old master painting in a modern museum, we usually see it under bright, even electric light designed to reveal every detail. It is easy to assume that this is the ideal way to view the work, the way its creator would have wanted. Yet for most of the history of European painting, artists worked and their patrons looked at pictures under very different conditions: the shifting glow of daylight through windows, or the warm, flickering light of candles and oil lamps. Painters were well aware of these conditions and (a)[adapted] their techniques to them. Gold leaf in religious altarpieces, for example, was not mere decoration; in a dim church lit by candles, it caught and multiplied the moving flames, making holy figures appear to shimmer with a light of their own. Similarly, the deep shadows and sharp highlights favored by many seventeenth-century painters gained a dramatic (b)[intensity] when seen in a darkened room, where the surrounding gloom blended with the darkness of the canvas itself. Under uniform museum lighting, such effects are often (c)[flattened]. Gold can look merely shiny, and carefully graded shadows may read as simple patches of black. Some art historians and curators have therefore begun experimenting with lighting that (d)[ignores] historical conditions, using dimmable lamps that imitate the color and movement of candlelight. Visitors who have seen familiar works displayed this way often report that the paintings seem to come alive, revealing depths they had never noticed. Such experiments do not suggest that modern lighting is wrong, since it remains essential for study and preservation. They do remind us, however, that a painting is not a fixed object with a single correct appearance but an (e)[encounter] shaped by the light in which it is seen.
items.q: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Seeing by Candlelight: How Light Shapes the Art We See
Why Museums Should Ban Electric Lighting Entirely
The Forgotten Value of Gold in Medieval Trade
Restoring Faded Colors in Old Master Paintings
How Modern Painters Learned to Use Shadows
items.exp: 옛 그림은 촛불과 자연광 아래에서 보도록 그려졌고, 그림의 모습은 비추는 빛에 따라 달라진다는 내용이에요. 그래서 ①이 알맞아요. 글은 현대 조명이 틀렸다는 뜻이 아니라고 했으므로 ②는 지나쳐요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
items.exp: 촛불의 색과 움직임을 흉내 내는 조명을 실험한다고 했으므로 역사적 조건을 무시하는(ignores) 것이 아니라 재현하는(recreates) 조명이어야 해요. 나머지는 빛에 맞춘 기법, 어둠 속의 강렬함, 균일한 조명에서 밋밋해지는 효과, 빛에 따라 달라지는 만남이라는 흐름에 맞아요.

items.passage:
(A)
Two days before the regional youth competition, Mira slipped on the icy steps outside the music school, and her violin case flew from her hand. When she opened it on the pavement, her worst fear was confirmed: the neck had snapped cleanly away from the body, and the strings hung loose like broken threads. The instrument had belonged to her grandmother, and Mira had played nothing else for eight years. Her teacher gave (a)[her] the name of an old repairman across the city, though he warned that such damage usually took weeks to mend.

(B)
On the day of the competition, Mira walked onto the stage with the plain violin and played as if it were an old friend. She did not win first prize, but one of the judges sought her out afterward to praise the warmth of her slow movement. A week later, she returned to the workshop, where her grandmother's violin lay repaired on the bench, the crack nearly invisible. When Mr. Halvorsen handed it to (b)[her], Mira hesitated, then asked whether she might come back sometimes to learn how instruments like these were made.

(C)
The workshop was a narrow room smelling of varnish and wood shavings. Mr. Halvorsen, a stooped man with gentle hands, turned the broken violin over slowly under his lamp. "The break is clean, which is good news," (c)[he] said at last. "But the glue must cure for at least a week, or the neck will fail under the tension of the strings." Mira felt her throat tighten. Seeing her expression, he reached up to a shelf and took down a dark, plain-looking violin. "Borrow this one. It is not beautiful, but it is honest. Come back after your competition."

(D)
At home that night, Mira found the borrowed violin stubborn and unfamiliar. Its tone was darker than her grandmother's, and passages that had once flowed easily now seemed to fight against (d)[her] fingers. Close to tears, she nearly decided to withdraw from the competition. Then she remembered the old man's word: honest. She stopped trying to make the instrument sound like the one she had lost and began listening to what it could do instead. By the next evening, the slow movement of her piece had taken on a richer, deeper color than (e)[she] had ever produced before.
items.q: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.exp: 수리공 이름을 받은 (A) 뒤에 작업실을 찾아가 바이올린을 빌리는 (C)가 와요. 그날 밤 빌린 악기로 연습하는 (D)가 이어지고, 대회 당일과 일주일 뒤 작업실에 다시 가는 (B)가 마지막이에요.
